name: Royal Manas National Park
blurb: Tall grass, tigers, rhinos and rare langurs on the Manas floodplain.

tip.title: Lose the tall grass
tip.text: Tall wet grassland shelters pygmy hogs, hog deer and floricans. Cut Tall grasses and watch them, then the tiger and leopard, respond.

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Royal Manas National Park, Manas National Park, Gee's golden langur). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.desc: Warm subtropical sun fuels fast growth of grasses and forest trees through the long wet season.
Heavy rain falls between May and September, about 333 cm a year in the Manas area, and drives growth and flooding.
Fungi, bacteria and insects break down dead grass, leaves and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.
A small deer of tall, moist grassland. It is a recorded tiger and leopard prey species here.
A large deer of the forest and its edges, recorded in the park and eaten by tigers and leopards.
Large grazing bovine of the grassland, which is listed among the herbivores of the Manas area.
Eats grass, browse and the invasive Siam weed. Its feeding and trampling shape open ground in forest and grassland.
A grassland grazer; Royal Manas is the only Bhutanese park where it lives.
Rooting omnivore recorded in the park and listed as tiger and leopard prey in GloBI.
A large constrictor. Wikipedia says pythons are among the predators of pygmy hogs.
A large ground lizard that eats insects, small mammals including hares, and scavenges carcasses such as deer.
Omnivore of forest and edges; GloBI records it eating Indian hares.
Top predator, recorded taking hog deer, sambar, wild boar, buffalo and hares in GloBI, and pygmy hogs per Wikipedia.
Apex predator of forest and grassland edge. GloBI records it eating deer, boar, hares, civets and golden langurs.

story: Royal Manas National Park is Bhutan's oldest national park, at 1,057 km². The government calls it the conservation showpiece of the Kingdom. It directly abuts Manas National Park in Assam, India, a World Heritage Site.
matters: Habitats range from lowland tropical forest to permanent ice fields. Across the border, Manas is known for rare wildlife such as the golden langur and pygmy hog.
